mission_05: Great work implementing a complete speaker diarization system! You now understand how audio recordings with multiple speakers can be automatically segmented and labeled by speaker identity. The x-vector embedding approach compresses variable-length speech segments into fixed-dimensional representations that capture speaker characteristics. Cosine similarity between these embeddings reveals which segments likely come from the same speaker. Spectral clustering leverages the graph structure of the similarity matrix, using eigenvectors of the Laplacian to find a low-dimensional representation where k-means clustering is more effective. The automatic speaker count estimation using eigenvalue gaps is a practical technique that avoids requiring this information as input. The Diarization Error Rate provides a standardized metric for evaluating diarization quality. This pipeline is directly applicable to meeting transcription, call center analytics, and broadcast news processing where identifying individual speakers is essential for downstream analysis.
